rounds.text: Chennai Petroleum Corporation Ltd is severely under-appreciated by the market, trading at an extraordinary bargain P/E of just 3.53x compared to a sector benchmark of 11.8x [E1, E6]. This low valuation is starkly disconnected from its elite profitability, demonstrated by a stellar return on equity of 41.95% and an exceptional return on capital employed of 46.92%, both vastly outperforming sector benchmarks [E9, E10]. Operational efficiency is at an all-time high, underscored by record crude throughput reaching 112% of installed capacity and a highest-ever distillate yield of 79.1% [E88, E90]. Furthermore, the company rewards shareholders handsomely, offering a robust dividend yield of 4.58% supported by a healthy 31.5% payout track record [E4, E63]. Conceded: compounded sales and profit growth over the last 3 years show minor contractions of -6% and -4% respectively [E16, E20]. Nevertheless, trailing twelve-month profit growth has rebounded dramatically by 387%, while institutional money flow remains positive with foreign holding increasing [E21, E44].

Despite headline financial numbers, Chennai Petroleum Corporation Ltd carries severe cyclical vulnerabilities and growth deceleration that the current valuation fails to fully price in. Long-term performance reveals sharp inconsistencies, notably a 3-year compounded sales growth of -6% [E16] and a 3-year compounded profit growth of -4% [E20], alongside an explicitly flagged screen warning that earnings growth is decelerating [E69]. Operational stability is further threatened by historical volatility, evidenced by a devastating worst peak-to-trough drawdown of -89.2% [E53], alongside ongoing structural headwinds including logistical constraints, crude oil price volatility [E94], and short-term supply disruptions affecting up to 40% of Middle East crude supply over brief periods [E95]. Furthermore, borrowings have ticked upward to Rs 2,202 Cr in Sep 2026 compared to Rs 1,964 Cr a year earlier [E39], and upcoming maintenance and inspection shutdowns will incur startup and shutdown costs that keep operating expenses elevated [E96]. Conceded: the company achieved a record annual crude throughput of 11.71 MMT at 112% capacity [E88], highest-ever distillate yield [E90], and a robust TTM operating margin expansion to 10% [E30]. Nevertheless, the yearly operating-margin trend remains officially classified as inconsistent over the last 3 years [E32], exposing investors to severe margin compression if regional refining margins retreat from recent peaks.

The bear highlights negative 3-year compounded sales growth of -6% [E16] and profit growth of -4% [E20], but ignores the powerful recent acceleration including a 31% TTM sales surge [E17] and a staggering 387% TTM profit growth [E21]. While the -89.2% historical drawdown [E53] and volatile Middle East crude supply [E95] represent past risks, the company operates from a conservatively financed position with a debt-to-equity ratio of just 0.16x [E37] and positive institutional money flow [E44]. Conceded: borrowings ticked upward to Rs 2,202 Cr [E39] and the 3-year operating-margin trend is inconsistent [E32], but these are heavily countered by a robust TTM operating margin expansion to 10% [E30] and a quarterly operating margin reaching 16% in Sep 2026 [E31]. Furthermore, upcoming maintenance shutdowns [E96] are entirely normal operational hurdles for a refinery achieving record-breaking annual crude throughput of 11.71 MMT at 112% capacity [E88] and highest-ever distillate yields [E90].

Conceded: the company achieved record crude throughput of 11.71 MMT at 112% capacity [E88] and highest-ever distillate yields [E90], while operating from a conservatively financed position with a debt-to-equity ratio of 0.16x [E37]. However, pointing to TTM sales and profit surges [E17, E21] ignores the persistent structural stagnation shown by 3-year compounded sales growth of -6% [E16] and profit growth of -4% [E20]. Furthermore, dismissing the inconsistent yearly and quarterly operating-margin trends [E32, E33] as mere noise overlooks the reality that maintenance and inspection shutdowns create startup and shutdown costs that keep operating expenses elevated [E96]. While institutional money flow reads positive [E44], borrowings have climbed to Rs 2,202 Cr in Sep 2026 from Rs 1,964 Cr a year prior [E39], and the historical peak-to-trough drawdown of -89.2% [E53] highlights severe cyclical vulnerability beneath any short-term margin expansion.

The bear’s focus on 3-year compounded growth [E16, E20] ignores the company’s current trajectory, where trailing twelve-month sales growth of 31% [E17] and profit growth of 387% [E21] demonstrate a powerful, recent operational turnaround. While the bear cites inconsistent margin trends [E32, E33], it fails to acknowledge the significant recent expansion, with quarterly operating margins jumping from 7% to 16% in just one year [E31]. Conceded: maintenance and inspection shutdowns do create temporary startup costs [E96], but these are part of a broader strategy to sustain record-breaking performance, such as achieving 112% of installed capacity [E88] and record distillate yields [E90]. The concern regarding rising borrowings [E39] is overstated given the company’s conservative debt-to-equity ratio of 0.16x [E37] and the fact that net borrowings remain below Rs 1,000 Cr [E91]. Finally, citing a historical drawdown [E53] ignores the current fundamental strength, where the company is actively deploying capital into high-growth projects like the 250 KTPA LOBS capacity addition [E84] and retail expansion [E77], supported by a sector-leading ROE of 41.95% [E9].

The bull’s reliance on trailing twelve-month growth [E17, E21] is a classic trap of extrapolating from a volatile base, as evidenced by the negative compounded sales and profit growth over the last three years [E16, E20]. While the bull highlights a recent jump in operating margins [E31], it ignores the reality that the company’s yearly and quarterly margin trends are explicitly classified as inconsistent [E32, E33]. Conceded: the company achieved record throughput [E88] and distillate yields [E90], but these operational peaks are inherently cyclical and subject to the very logistical constraints and crude price volatility that management admits pose ongoing challenges [E94]. The bull dismisses rising borrowings [E39] by pointing to a current ratio, yet the data provider explicitly warns that this ratio of 1.43x provides only an adequate but thin buffer [E38]. Furthermore, the bull’s focus on current ROE [E9] ignores the historical context of a massive -89.2% peak-to-trough drawdown [E53], which serves as a stark reminder of the risks inherent in this sector. Finally, while the bull celebrates the capital expenditure on LOBS and retail projects [E77, E84], it fails to account for the fact that these projects are in a build-up phase [E40] that will require sustained, heavy investment [E76] while the company simultaneously faces elevated operating costs from scheduled maintenance and inspection shutdowns [E96].

CPCL expects to incur INR 2,000 crores over 2 to 3 years on LOBS and retail projects, along with ~INR 500 crores in normal annual capex.
evidence.quote: LOBS project, Group 2, Group 3 LOBS project is INR1,600 crores. The retail outlet project is INR400 crores. So that makes it INR2,000 crores. This INR2,000 crores will happen over 2 to 3 years. Besides, every year, you can assume another INR500 crores is our normal capex.

evidence.fact: CPCL expects a lot of commissioning from its retail outlet expansion during FY 2026-27.
evidence.quote: Even our retail outlet endeavor for which we had taken 300 licenses has started. And this year, that is '26-'27, we'll see a lot of commissioning out of them.

evidence.fact: Management stated there is no M&I in the first 6 months, but a scheduled M&I of one refinery unit is planned close to September or October.
evidence.quote: First, reply to you , in the first 6 months, we don't see any M&I. So it may not be there. But yes, maybe close to September, October, we have a scheduled M&I of one of our refinery units.

evidence.fact: CPCL sells close to 90% of its products under long-term agreement to Indian Oil at refinery transfer price (RTP).
evidence.quote: No, our agreement, as you would be aware, close to about 90% of our product, mostly HSD, MS, goes to Indian Oil. We have a tie-up with them, we've a long-term agreement with them for selling. And the agreement is at RTP, that is refinery transfer price.

evidence.fact: There is a shortfall of motor spirit (MS) in the southern market of around 20 TMT per month where production is lower than demand.
evidence.quote: MS in southern market, there is a clear shortfall so, the production is less than demand. It is close to about 20 TMT per month.

evidence.fact: Demand growth forecast in the southern market is around 4%-5% for MS and 3% for HSD.
evidence.quote: Like MS, they are projecting 6% and here we see around 4%-5%. HSD we see at 3% growth forecast, as against 2.5% odd here.

evidence.fact: CPCL incurred capex of INR 856 crores in FY26 compared to INR 673 crores in the previous year.
evidence.quote: During the current year, the capex was INR856 crores as compared to INR673 crores in the previous year.

evidence.fact: Execution of the Group 2, Group 3 LOBS project has started in full swing.
evidence.quote: Some of the important projects that we'll be taking up is Group 2, Group 3 LOBS for which all approvals are in place and the project execution has started in full swing.

evidence.fact: The new LOBS project will add 250 KTPA capacity in Group 2 and Group 3 grades.
evidence.quote: My new unit will take me to a 250,000, 250 KTPA in Group 2, Group 3 capacity, and that will be a fresh addition.

evidence.fact: Q4 FY26 GRM stood at $13.75 per barrel compared to Singapore benchmark of $8.70 per barrel.
evidence.quote: The GRM for quarter 4 was $13.75 barrel as compared to Singapore benchmark of $8.70 per barrel, which again reiterates that all these efficiencies are constant, continuous and are being sustained over each period.

evidence.fact: Core GRM for Q4 FY26 was $10.3 per barrel.
evidence.quote: 10.3 $/bbl would be the core GRM.

evidence.fact: Forex loss was approximately INR 200 crores for Q4 and around INR 350 crores for the full year.
evidence.quote: For the quarter, it would be for the quarter, it is approximately INR 200 crores,. And for the whole year, it will be around INR350 crores.

evidence.fact: CPCL achieved a record annual crude throughput of 11.71 MMT, representing 112% of installed capacity.
evidence.quote: CPCL achieved a highest ever crude throughput of 11.71 MMT, million metric ton, which equivalents to 112% of installed capacity, breaking records of our previous best of 11.64 MMT achieved in financial year 2023-'24.

evidence.fact: Q4 FY26 crude throughput reached 2.93 MMT, equivalent to 111% of installed capacity.
evidence.quote: In quarter 4 of the current financial year, CPCL achieved a crude throughput of 2.93 MMT, which is also 111% of installed capacity.

evidence.fact: CPCL achieved a record distillate yield of 79.1% during the financial year.
evidence.quote: Further, highest ever distillate yield of 79.1%, beating our previous record of 77.6% set in 2019-'20 was also achieved during this year.

evidence.fact: CPCL reported gross borrowings of INR 1,900 crores and net borrowings of INR 973 crores.
evidence.quote: On a gross basis, the borrowings are INR1,900 crores, but on a net basis, it is less than INR1,000 crores, to be precise, INR973 crores.

evidence.fact: CPCL recommended a final dividend of INR 54 per share in addition to an interim dividend of INR 8 per share, totaling INR 62 per share.
evidence.quote: During the year, for the first time, CPCL paid an interim dividend, and we are happy to announce that in addition to the interim dividend of INR8 per equity share of INR10 each, the Board has recommended a final dividend of INR54 per share, taking the total dividend for the year to INR62 per share, which again is highest ever.

evidence.fact: Debt to equity ratio stood at 0.39 as of March 31, 2025, with total debt at Rs. 3,100 crores.
evidence.quote: When I turn to leverage position, the debt equity position as on March 31, 2025, is 0.39 compared to 0.32 in the previous year. At an absolute level, the debt stands at Rs. 3,100 crores as compared to Rs. 2,762 crores as on March 31, 2024.

evidence.fact: Logistical constraints and crude oil price volatility present ongoing operational challenges.
evidence.quote: Now with all this, I would like to say the uncertainties due to logistical constraints, volatility of crude oil prices do pose challenges.

evidence.fact: Short-term supply disruptions affected 30% to 40% of Middle East crude supply over a brief period.
evidence.quote: What has impacted is that maybe 30% to 40% was affected over a very short period, but all have assured us that depending on the situation, they will make up all the cargoes.

evidence.fact: Maintenance and inspection shutdowns lead to startup and shutdown costs that keep operating costs temporarily elevated.
evidence.quote: Plus, every M&I shutdown also involves startup and shutdown cost. So, the operating cost also remains little elevated.

evidence.fact: Management commitment (FY27): CPCL expects commissioning out of its retail outlet project with 300 licenses in FY 2026-27.
evidence.quote: Even our retail outlet endeavor for which we had taken 300 licenses has started. And this year, that is '26-'27, we'll see a lot of commissioning out of them.

evidence.fact: Management commitment (next 2 years): CPCL plans to incur INR 2,000 crores across its LOBS and retail outlet projects over 2 to 3 years.
evidence.quote: LOBS project, Group 2, Group 3 LOBS project is INR1,600 crores. The retail outlet project is INR400 crores. So that makes it INR2,000 crores. This INR2,000 crores will happen over 2 to 3 years.

evidence.fact: Management commitment (next 2 years): Normal maintenance CAPEX is expected to be around Rs. 250 to Rs. 300 crores annually over the next two years.
evidence.quote: The normal maintenance CAPEX for the next two years would be around Rs. 250 to Rs. 300 crores, maintenance CAPEX plus small regular CAPEX normally.
